consumer: The engine condition/dialogue eligibility check built by conditional_t::set_has_item, which asks the yes/no question 'does the character actor possess item c4?' via actor->charges_of(c4)>0 || actor->has_amount(c4,1).
scope: only the character's own carried/possessed items (wielded, worn, inventory, recursing into containers per visit_items but NOT into gun/magazine contents); not nearby-reachable items, not a map region.
decisive_source: src/condition.cpp::conditional_t<T>::set_has_item -- its body returns the boolean actor->charges_of(item_id)>0 || actor->has_amount(item_id,1), the engine-computed possession predicate over the character actor that conditions consume.
divergence: The avatar's only c4 is tucked inside a wielded gun's or a magazine's contents: visit_internal (visitable.cpp) deliberately does NOT recurse into gun/magazine contents, so the engine predicate returns false, while a re-derivation that flattens or scans the avatar.carried_items[] snapshot for type_id=='c4' would wrongly report true.
